package_info.package_versions: All Python versions supporting sitecustomize/usercustomize modules (e.g., Python 3.x)
package_info.why_malicious: The technique abuses Python's automatic import of usercustomize.py and sitecustomize.py modules from site-packages directories to achieve persistent, stealthy code execution on every Python interpreter invocation. This allows arbitrary code (including malware) to run repeatedly, acting as a backdoor and persistence mechanism, without user awareness.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: print("[!] Malware could have run here")
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code executes arbitrary Python instructions (here, a print statement, but could be any payload) every time the interpreter starts, enabling persistent execution of malicious logic.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Code in usercustomize.py is executed automatically on every Python interpreter start, regardless of the script being run. Attackers can use this to persistently execute malicious code without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Python packages should not execute arbitrary code on every interpreter invocation outside their intended use. This behavior subverts user expectations and standard package operation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use includes customizing the Python environment for user-specific needs (e.g., setting up sys.path or environment variables), but not for persistent, hidden code execution.
key_indicators: Presence of usercustomize.py in user site-packages directory

attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent execution of malicious code on every Python interpreter invocation.

attack_chain.action: Every time the Python interpreter is started, the malicious code in usercustomize.py or sitecustomize.py is automatically executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor/persistence: attacker code runs repeatedly, can exfiltrate data or perform other malicious actions.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the creation or modification of usercustomize.py and sitecustomize.py files in all site-packages directories. Flag any non-standard or unauthorized code in these files, especially if it initiates network connections or accesses sensitive data. Use file integrity monitoring and alert on changes. Review Python interpreter startup logs for unexpected output or behavior. Consider restricting write permissions to site-packages directories and using interpreter options (-S, -s, or PYTHONNOUSERSITE) in sensitive environments.
